notable_absence.finding: The Legacy Durability section links to the Scala SDK's API documentation for `PersistTo`/`ReplicateTo' (https://docs.couchbase.com/sdk-api/couchbase-scala-client/...), not to any Java SDK API reference - an apparent copy-paste artifact from a shared cross-SDK doc source, on a page that is otherwise entirely Java-SDK-specific.

cross_component_finding: This page's KV-write ambiguity scenario (network drop between server-side success and client-side acknowledgement, leaving the client unable to tell whether the operation succeeded) is structurally the SAME class of problem that the promoted sdk:transaction-error-handling formalises as a first-class, catchable TransactionCommitAmbiguousException at the whole-transaction scope. At this page's single-KV-write scope, however, Couchbase raises no distinct typed exception at all for it - the page only describes the scenario in prose and offers two mitigations: simply retry (if idempotent) or switch to distributed transactions (if not). This is a third confirmation of the round's cross-scope hypothesis: not just the DurabilityLevel enum (sharesOptionSetWith) but the AMBIGUITY FAILURE MODE ITSELF recurs at both the KV-durability and transaction layers, and only the transaction layer promotes it to a formal exception type.
cross_product_finding: The Legacy Durability section's cross-link to the Scala SDK's (not the Java SDK's) API documentation for PersistTo/ReplicateTo suggests this particular subsection is shared boilerplate reused verbatim across multiple Couchbase SDK doc sets rather than authored per-SDK - a content-provenance signal distinct from the deliberate cross-product design choices (Capella vs self-managed prerequisite divergence, AZ-egress-cost features) found elsewhere in this batch.
